newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ dlr likely to stay down for months.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ dlr likely to stay down for months.

text.p: Treasurer Winston Peters said on Friday the New Zealand dollar was likely to stay down for some months in the wake of its recent slide.
"The dollar has been falling and is likely to stay down for some months yet," he said in speech notes for an address to the Export Institute of New Zealand for delivery in Tauranga.
Peters said the government was attempting to support the export sector.
Much had been made in recent weeks of the high value of the New Zealand dollar and how that had unfairly punished exporters, he said.
He reiterated recent comments from Finance Minister Bill Birch that exporters had maintained their export levels despite two years of hard times.

"The government believes exporters are in a strong position to bounce back after the recent fall in the value of the currency, because you've toughened yourselves up while the dollar was high," Peters said.
The New Zealand dollar has fallen nearly 10 percent against the U.S. dollar to 64.50 U.S. cents from a peak of 71.5 cents since November.
"Now it (the kiwi dollar) is dropping, you're in a superb position to take full advantage of your competitive advantage. We're doing all we can to remove the obstacles from your path," Peters said.
